route_A_bounded_initial_permission.mechanism: pass seconds= into PreparedGovernance.reserve, derived from the Job's own resolved boundaries
route_A_bounded_initial_permission.the_obstacle: a single number per attempt has to assume HOW MANY invocations one attempt may make. 3600 + 900 = 4500 is only correct for one provider turn plus one verification.
route_A_bounded_initial_permission.and_the_project_says_that_count_is_an_AS: revision-4/inputs/policy.json, verbatim: "No product cumulative ceiling. Operator observes a proposed 9900s window; 9000s assumes one provider and one verification invocation per stage." The review repeats it: neither 9000 nor 9900 can become an absolute execution cap.
route_A_bounded_initial_permission.therefore: choosing a per-attempt total means pinning an invocation-count policy nobody has pinned. That is the shape of decision the review says to return rather than invent.

route_B_timely_eligible_renewal.mechanism: the accepted W333485 renewal: the token starts at its ordinary lifetime and is renewed while the attempt is legitimately still working, bounded by RENEWAL_LIMIT
route_B_timely_eligible_renewal.why_it_may_need_NO_new_policy: it declares no total and assumes no invocation count; the bound is the existing renewal limit, and 900 x (1 + 4) covers 3600 + 900 WITHOUT anyone declaring 4500 as a cap
route_B_timely_eligible_renewal.what_it_requires_and_I_DID_NOT_PROVE: a renewer on the native serving path -- something in tools/job_manager serving that calls tokens.renew on a timely basis for a live attempt, the way the authoring controller's Lane.tick did. Whether the native loop has that, or whether it is the demonstrated missing connection, is UNVERIFIED by me.
route_B_timely_eligible_renewal.and_the_PLAN_already_permits_it: current PLAN: "Renewal is optional as a mechanism; actual timely eligible renewal OR appropriate bounded initial permission satisfies TOK-9."
